alex-karp.position: State power, including military strength, is what makes it possible to defend individual liberty.
alex-karp.quote: The privilege to engage in defending the individual against state power is made possible by state power itself.
alex-karp.work: In Defense of Europe (A Letter from the Chief Executive Officer)

alex-karp.position: Technology companies have a duty to equip their nation's soldiers and security agencies.
alex-karp.quote: Our software is used to target terrorists and to keep soldiers safe. If we are going to ask someone to put themselves in harm’s way, we believe that we have a duty to give them what they need to do their job.
alex-karp.work: Letter from the Chief Executive Officer (Palantir S-1)

alex-karp.position: Software can be built to constrain government surveillance as well as to support security.
alex-karp.quote: It is confounding to many that the same software system that is capable of preventing a terror attack may be equally capable of preventing an unconstitutional intrusion into the private lives of citizens by the state.

alex-karp.position: Silicon Valley engineers should not decide the moral questions raised by how technology is used.
alex-karp.quote: The engineering elite of Silicon Valley may know more than most about building software. But they do not know more about how society should be organized or what justice requires.
alex-karp.work: Letter from the Chief Executive Officer (Palantir S-1)

alex-karp.position: Language models create value only when grounded in real-world data and operations.
alex-karp.quote: The large language models alone will not lead us to salvation.

alex-karp.position: AI should be judged by the measurable results it delivers, not by talk about its future.
alex-karp.quote: Anything lacking a zealous focus on the value being created by these technical systems, the mice that the cat actually catches, will ultimately fade to gray and be forgotten.

alondra-nelson.position: The purpose of AI should be to benefit people, not efficiency or scale for their own sake.
alondra-nelson.quote: The purpose of AI is not scale or efficiency. The purpose of AI is people.
alondra-nelson.work: Three Fallacies: Alondra Nelson's Remarks at Élysée Palace on the Occasion of the AI Action Summit

alondra-nelson.position: Careful governance and innovation are not in conflict; good rules can spur innovation.
alondra-nelson.quote: The author’s experience developing the AI Bill of Rights made evident that thoughtful constraints often spark more meaningful innovation by directing creative energy toward socially beneficial outcomes.
alondra-nelson.work: Regulating AI in the Evolving Transatlantic Landscape

alondra-nelson.position: People affected by automated systems should have protections, including the ability to reach a human alternative.
alondra-nelson.quote: You should be able to opt out from automated systems in favor of a human alternative, where appropriate.
alondra-nelson.work: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights

alondra-nelson.position: The broad public, not only technical experts, should have a say in how AI is built and used.
alondra-nelson.quote: the people who have to adopt these technologies need to understand that they have a say.
alondra-nelson.work: A Conversation with Dr. Alondra Nelson on AI and Democracy

alondra-nelson.position: Science and technology policy runs through every other policy area rather than sitting apart from them.
alondra-nelson.quote: In print have got to get better at understanding and creating policy that appreciates that science and technology really sit at the center of all domestic and international policy issues.
alondra-nelson.work: A Conversation with Dr. Alondra Nelson on AI and Democracy

alondra-nelson.position: Using AI in government requires accountability and transparency to the public.
alondra-nelson.quote: One of the things that AI does is create more black boxes or bigger, denser black boxes about processes that make it harder to have accountability and transparency. I think that's a terrible thing for government.
alondra-nelson.work: A Conversation with Dr. Alondra Nelson on AI and Democracy

andrej-karpathy.position: LLMs are a new computing paradigm in which prompts and context act as the program and the model acts as the interpreter.
andrej-karpathy.quote: Software 3.0 is about programming through prompting. What's in the context window is your lever over the interpreter, and the interpreter is the LLM.

andrej-karpathy.position: AI automates tasks fastest where results can be automatically checked, which explains its uneven progress.
andrej-karpathy.quote: The more a task/job is verifiable, the more amenable it is to automation in the new programming paradigm.

andrej-karpathy.position: LLMs are a distinct, non-animal kind of intelligence, shaped by imitating human text and by commercial optimization rather than evolution.
andrej-karpathy.quote: LLMs are shaped a lot less by biological evolution and a lot more by commercial evolution.

andrej-karpathy.position: Because AI capabilities are uneven, people should stay in the loop and supervise what models do.
andrej-karpathy.quote: To the extent models remain jagged, it means you need to be in the loop. You need to treat them as tools and stay in touch with what they are doing.

andrej-karpathy.position: Unlike most earlier technologies, LLMs have so far benefited ordinary individuals more than corporations and governments.
andrej-karpathy.quote: they generate disproportionate benefit for regular people, while their impact is a lot more muted and lagging in corporations and governments.
andrej-karpathy.work: Power to the people: How LLMs flip the script on technology diffusion

andrej-karpathy.position: Advanced AI and superintelligence will arrive as a gradual continuation of ongoing automation rather than a sudden break.
andrej-karpathy.quote: I see it as a progression of automation in society. Extrapolating the trend of computing, there will be a gradual automation of a lot of things, and superintelligence will an extrapolation of that.
andrej-karpathy.work: Andrej Karpathy: AGI is still a decade away

anton-korinek.position: Wages depend on a race between automation and capital accumulation, rising with some automation and falling near full automation.
anton-korinek.quote: If we have just a little bit of automation, then more automation helps workers. if we already have a lot of automation, and in particular, as we approach the very last tasks left for humans, then automation hurts workers.
anton-korinek.work: Anton Korinek on Automating Work and the Economics of an Intelligence Explosion

anton-korinek.position: If human task ability is bounded and full automation arrives, wages collapse.
anton-korinek.quote: By contrast, if the complexity of tasks that humans can perform is bounded and full automation is reached, then wages collapse.
anton-korinek.work: Scenarios for the Transition to AGI

anton-korinek.position: Policymakers should plan across several AI scenarios, including near-term AGI, rather than betting on one.
anton-korinek.quote: Adopt a portfolio approach: hedge across multiple scenarios rather than planning for a single outcome.
anton-korinek.work: Scenario Planning for an A(G)I Future

anton-korinek.position: Income distribution will need to move away from relying mainly on wages from work.
anton-korinek.quote: So I think we need to fundamentally rethink our systems of income distribution.
anton-korinek.work: Transcript of Anton Korinek on What Happens When AI Replaces Every Job?

anton-korinek.position: A small basic income should be set up now so it can scale if mass displacement comes.
anton-korinek.quote: I just want the infrastructure in place. It could be 10 bucks a month just to have the system operating.
anton-korinek.work: Anton Korinek on Automating Work and the Economics of an Intelligence Explosion

anton-korinek.position: Advanced AI carries a greater risk of power concentration than any past technology.
anton-korinek.quote: Now, I will say that in the case of AI, the risk of power concentration is probably different and much more significant than with any other technology in the past.
anton-korinek.work: Anton Korinek on Automating Work and the Economics of an Intelligence Explosion

arvind-narayanan.position: AI is a transformative but normal general-purpose technology, comparable to electricity or the internet.
arvind-narayanan.quote: To view AI as normal is not to understate its impact—even transformative, general-purpose technologies such as electricity and the internet are “normal” in our conception.

arvind-narayanan.position: AI's economic impact will arrive through slow diffusion over decades, not through sudden capability jumps.
arvind-narayanan.quote: Diffusion occurs at human (and societal) timescales, not at the speed of tech development.

arvind-narayanan.position: An AI system's capability is distinct from its power, which depends on how humans design the systems it operates in.
arvind-narayanan.quote: Capability is an intrinsic property of an AI system, whereas power is a matter of how we design the environment in which AI systems operate.

arvind-narayanan.position: Building societal resilience is a better defense against AI misuse than nonproliferation or restrictions on releases.
arvind-narayanan.quote: If the most that nonproliferation can buy us is a few months, the urgent priority should be investing in resilience so that we are better prepared when those capabilities inevitably become widely available, as we discuss below.
arvind-narayanan.work: Do AI Risks Require Extraordinary Government Intervention?

arvind-narayanan.position: Probability estimates of AI-caused extinction are too unreliable to guide public policy.
arvind-narayanan.quote: Our central claim is that AI x-risk forecasts are far too unreliable to be useful for policy, and in fact highly misleading.
arvind-narayanan.work: AI existential risk probabilities are too unreliable to inform policy

arvind-narayanan.position: Humans augmented by AI should remain more capable than AI systems acting alone, and should stay in control.
arvind-narayanan.quote: I think we can ensure that we are the superintelligences of the future and we win that race, as opposed to allowing AI systems to act alone in ways that would threaten our future and control.
arvind-narayanan.work: What will be left for us to work on?

audrey-tang.position: Technology should reward ideas that bridge opposing groups, turning conflict into common ground.
audrey-tang.quote: We flipped the incentive for going viral from outrage to overlap.

audrey-tang.position: Engagement-maximizing recommendation algorithms drive polarization and should be replaced by pro-social designs.
audrey-tang.quote: It maximizes engagement. It maximized watch time, clicks, and it creates a parasitic recommendation engine: engagement through enragement.
audrey-tang.work: 2025-11-10 Berlin Freedom Conference: The Role of AI

audrey-tang.position: AI should be many bounded, local stewards under democratic authority rather than one system that manages everything.
audrey-tang.quote: We can design AIs to be local stewards — Kami of Care — whose boundedness is not intrinsic but engineered: resource caps, sunset timers, non-expansion pacts, and fresh democratic authority for any scope change.

audrey-tang.position: Citizens should deliberate themselves rather than delegate decisions to AI, even good AI.
audrey-tang.quote: If AI makes all the decisions for us—even good ones—our civic muscle atrophies.

audrey-tang.position: People should be able to move their data and social graph between platforms, so platforms compete on care.
audrey-tang.quote: The information superhighway must have off-ramps, which forces platforms to compete on quality of care, not lock-in.

audrey-tang.position: AI risk cannot be estimated meaningfully until models are interpretable.
audrey-tang.quote: The calculation simply does not converge unless you have real interpretability.
audrey-tang.work: 2026-01-20 Doom Debate (Doom Debates, with Liron Shapira)

balaji-srinivasan.position: There will be many strong AI models in balance, not one dominant AGI.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: First: there is no AGI, there are many AGIs.

balaji-srinivasan.position: Humans sense the world and set goals, while AI carries out the work.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: So humans are the sensor. AI is the actuator.
balaji-srinivasan.work: Why Balaji Srinivasan Thinks the SaaS Apocalypse Is Overhyped (a16z; published by a16z as 'Balaji on Why AI Raises the Cost of Verification')

balaji-srinivasan.position: AI makes content cheaper to generate but more costly to verify.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: AI does reduce the cost of generation but it increases the cost of verification
balaji-srinivasan.work: Why Balaji Srinivasan Thinks the SaaS Apocalypse Is Overhyped (a16z; published by a16z as 'Balaji on Why AI Raises the Cost of Verification')

balaji-srinivasan.position: Cryptography can constrain AI because crypto is deterministic and AI is probabilistic.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: AI is probabilistic while crypto is deterministic. So crypto can constrain AI.

balaji-srinivasan.position: New states can be built by starting with online communities and acquiring land later.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: Rather than starting with the physical territory, we start with the digital community.
balaji-srinivasan.work: The Network State in One Essay

balaji-srinivasan.position: Technology exists to reduce scarcity, and its ultimate purpose is to end mortality.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: If the proximate purpose of technology is to reduce scarcity, the ultimate purpose of technology is to eliminate mortality.

bernie-sanders.position: AI and robotics are likely to displace very large numbers of blue-collar and white-collar workers.
bernie-sanders.quote: And, if you’re currently in the workforce, there’s a good chance it will take your job.
bernie-sanders.work: Artificial intelligence is coming for the working class. We must fight back

bernie-sanders.position: Billionaire tech leaders are pushing AI mainly to increase their own wealth and power.
bernie-sanders.quote: They are implementing a technology that will make them and their corporate clients even richer and more powerful.
bernie-sanders.work: Artificial intelligence is coming for the working class. We must fight back

bernie-sanders.position: Productivity gains from AI should bring a shorter workweek with no loss in pay.
bernie-sanders.quote: It means that as productivity greatly increases, the workweek should be significantly reduced with no loss in pay.
bernie-sanders.work: Artificial intelligence is coming for the working class. We must fight back

bernie-sanders.position: If AI creates great wealth, the nation should guarantee everyone housing, health care and education.
bernie-sanders.quote: If AI and robotics are going to create unprecedented wealth, we as a nation must guarantee all Americans a high-quality standard of living: decent housing, health care, education, and more.
bernie-sanders.work: Artificial intelligence is coming for the working class. We must fight back

bernie-sanders.position: Humans should remain in control, and transhumanist aims to replace or surpass humanity should be rejected.
bernie-sanders.quote: Human beings, not machines, must come first.
bernie-sanders.work: Don't Let Big Tech Dictate Humanity's Future

brian-merchant.position: The original Luddites opposed exploitative uses of machinery, not technology itself.
brian-merchant.quote: The Luddites were not against progress or anti-technology. They were against exploitation; they were anti-poverty.
brian-merchant.work: Understanding the Luddites in the age of AI

brian-merchant.position: AI's effect on jobs comes from management decisions to cut labor costs and consolidate control.
brian-merchant.quote: It’s a series of management decisions being made by executives seeking to cut labor costs and consolidate control in their organizations.
brian-merchant.work: The AI jobs crisis is here, now

brian-merchant.position: Workers and users should have a real say over technologies that reshape their workplaces and communities.
brian-merchant.quote: Returning to the Luddites reminds us that above all, workers and users must have a seat at the table.
brian-merchant.work: Understanding the Luddites in the age of AI

brian-merchant.position: AI's main commercial value to investors lies in automating and controlling labor.
brian-merchant.quote: That prospect—of deskilling, controlling, or eliminating labor outright—is what made AI so uniquely valuable in the first place.
brian-merchant.work: Why the AI backlash has turned violent

brian-merchant.position: Leading AI companies concentrate wealth and power and lobby against democratic regulation of their products.
brian-merchant.quote: OpenAI has spent millions lobbying against laws it doesn’t like in California and the European Union, trying to avoid regulation, laws, and other inconvenient outcomes of democracy.
brian-merchant.work: Why the AI backlash has turned violent

curtis-yarvin.position: The main problem in human affairs is organized violence, which clear and unbreakable rules of ownership can prevent.
curtis-yarvin.quote: The basic idea of formalism is just that the main problem in human affairs is violence.

curtis-yarvin.position: Existing power should be formally recognized as ownership rather than redistributed according to who ought to have what.
curtis-yarvin.quote: Formalism says: let’s figure out exactly who has what, now, and give them a fancy little certificate.

curtis-yarvin.position: AI cannot threaten humanity because every virtual intelligence depends on humans who physically control it.
curtis-yarvin.quote: Every virtual intelligence physically depends on some physical intelligence.

curtis-yarvin.position: Humans remain fully responsible for whatever their machines, including AI, do.
curtis-yarvin.quote: Human responsibility is unimpaired by any chain of nonhuman intermediation.

curtis-yarvin.position: Large language models recognize patterns by intuition and do not reason.
curtis-yarvin.quote: LLMs do not think—they see and connect patterns. LLMs are not reasoning machines. They are intuition machines.

curtis-yarvin.position: Civilization depends on social order as well as technology, and technology alone does not sustain it.
curtis-yarvin.quote: The curve of technology matters—so does the curve of order.

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Leading AI companies are racing to build superintelligence by automating AI research itself.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: Their plan for how to get there is to automate the AI research and development process itself.

daniel-kokotajlo.position: The public and outside researchers need much more visibility into what frontier AI companies are doing.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: First, we need to dramatically improve transparency into the AI industry.

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Our ability to detect whether AI systems are misaligned is likely to decline as they grow more capable.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: Worse, our ability to notice misalignment problems in the first place is on track to decrease dramatically for three reasons.

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Developing AGI in secret risks both misaligned AI and power concentrated in a small group.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: I didn’t take concentration of power seriously enough as a problem.
daniel-kokotajlo.work: Training AGI in Secret would be Unsafe and Unethical

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Economic growth is a poor guide to AI timelines, because decisive AI effects may come before growth speeds up.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: I think world GDP (and economic growth more generally) is overrated as a metric for AI timelines and takeoff speeds.
daniel-kokotajlo.work: Against GDP as a metric for timelines and takeoff speeds

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Decision-makers should track separately when they hand trust to AI systems and when they hand over decisions.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: There are two importantly different kinds of handoff: Handing off trust and handing off decisionmaking.

dario-amodei.position: Powerful AI could greatly improve human life, including health and poverty, if its risks are handled.
dario-amodei.quote: In fact, one of my main reasons for focusing on risks is that they’re the only thing standing between us and what I see as a fundamentally positive future.

dario-amodei.position: Democracies should use AI to defend themselves and lead over autocracies.
dario-amodei.quote: I believe deeply in the existential importance of using AI to defend the United States and other democracies, and to defeat our autocratic adversaries.
dario-amodei.work: Statement from Dario Amodei on our discussions with the Department of War

dario-amodei.position: AI regulation should be judicious, simple and minimally burdensome, tightening as evidence grows.
dario-amodei.quote: It’s thus very important for regulations to be judicious: they should seek to avoid collateral damage, be as simple as possible, and impose the least burden necessary to get the job done.

dario-amodei.position: AI smarter than top experts in most fields may arrive within a few years.
dario-amodei.quote: As I wrote in Machines of Loving Grace, powerful AI could be as little as 1–2 years away, although it could also be considerably further out.

dario-amodei.position: AI should not be used for mass domestic surveillance.
dario-amodei.quote: But using these systems for mass domestic surveillance is incompatible with democratic values.
dario-amodei.work: Statement from Dario Amodei on our discussions with the Department of War

dario-amodei.position: AI risks should be discussed soberly and factually, avoiding doomerism.
dario-amodei.quote: The lesson is that we need to discuss and address risks in a realistic, pragmatic manner: sober, fact-based, and well equipped to survive changing tides.

daron-acemoglu.position: The direction of technological change is a social choice rather than a fixed path, so AI can be steered.
daron-acemoglu.quote: that there are many different things we can do with AI, and it's a choice what we do with AI.
daron-acemoglu.work: AI & the Future of Work w/ David Autor & Daron Acemoglu (The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart, transcript)

daron-acemoglu.position: Technological progress does not automatically bring broad prosperity; that depends on competition, worker power and the kind of technology developed.
daron-acemoglu.quote: there is nothing automatic about technological progress bringing widespread prosperity.
daron-acemoglu.work: Daron Acemoglu on Innovation and Shared Prosperity

daron-acemoglu.position: AI should be developed to make workers more productive and create new tasks, rather than mainly to automate work.
daron-acemoglu.quote: We can create AI that makes workers more productive rather than just automate their work.

daron-acemoglu.position: US tax policy favours capital over labor, which tilts firms toward automation and should be rebalanced.
daron-acemoglu.quote: Like, for example, in the United States, we tax labor heavily. We subsidize capital.
daron-acemoglu.work: AI & the Future of Work w/ David Autor & Daron Acemoglu (The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart, transcript)

daron-acemoglu.position: Concentrated power over AI held by a few large tech companies needs countervailing forces such as unions, regulators and civil society.
daron-acemoglu.work: Mindscape 283: Daron Acemoglu on Technology, Inequality, and Power

daron-acemoglu.position: AI's productivity gains over the next decade are likely to be modest.
daron-acemoglu.quote: So, 15% of 5% is equal to a boost to total factor productivity of around 0.75%.
daron-acemoglu.work: Have AI gains been overhyped? Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu talks to MoneyWeek

david-sacks.position: Predictions of a rapid takeoff to a single dominant superintelligence have not matched how AI is developing.
david-sacks.work: Long X post: the 'Goldilocks' state of AI and why the doomer narratives were wrong

david-sacks.position: Several competing AI companies, plus open source, keep power over AI from concentrating.
david-sacks.quote: So far, we have avoided a monopolistic outcome that vests all power and control in a single entity.
david-sacks.work: Long X post: the 'Goldilocks' state of AI and why the doomer narratives were wrong

david-sacks.position: The greatest AI danger is government and corporate power combining to censor and control information.
david-sacks.quote: In my view, the most likely dystopian outcome with AI is a marriage of corporate and state power similar to what we saw exposed in the Twitter Files, where “Trust & Safety” gets weaponized into government censorship and control.
david-sacks.work: Long X post: the 'Goldilocks' state of AI and why the doomer narratives were wrong

david-sacks.position: The United States should win the AI race by out-innovating its competitors.
david-sacks.quote: We win by out-innovating our competitors.
david-sacks.work: Thread on the White House AI Action Plan and Trump's first major AI speech

david-sacks.position: Current AI works best as a division of labor with humans, not as an autonomous replacement.
david-sacks.quote: There is also an increasingly clear division of labor between humans and AI.
david-sacks.work: Long X post: the 'Goldilocks' state of AI and why the doomer narratives were wrong

david-sacks.position: In foreign conflicts, the US should pursue diplomacy and avoid escalation.
david-sacks.quote: It’s deeply irresponsible not to try for diplomacy when the stakes are so high.
david-sacks.work: Should America Go All In on Ukraine?

dean-ball.position: Technology has been overwhelmingly good for human beings across history.
dean-ball.quote: I believe the net effect of technology on human beings has been not just modestly but overwhelmingly good, on average, throughout our history.
dean-ball.work: 2023 (Or, Why I am Not a Doomer)

dean-ball.position: Intelligence alone cannot overcome real-world limits such as experiments, so AI doom scenarios are doubtful.
dean-ball.quote: The implicit, and sometimes even explicit, argument of “the doomers” is that intelligence is the sole bottleneck on capability (because any other bottlenecks can be resolved with more intelligence), and that everything else follows instantly once that bottleneck is removed.
dean-ball.work: 2023 (Or, Why I am Not a Doomer)

dean-ball.position: The state has a limited, defined role in managing catastrophic risks from AI misuse.
dean-ball.quote: So I support regulations to try to mitigate the catastrophic risks of AI.
dean-ball.work: Before Leviathan Wakes (Why I Believe What I Believe)

dean-ball.position: Government-licensed private bodies should audit frontier AI labs, rather than government agencies doing it directly.
dean-ball.quote: Perhaps, if you are persuaded that private bodies have merit, you could imagine the government certifying or licensing the auditors, just as auditors in accounting are licensed.
dean-ball.work: What Should Be Done (35 thoughts on what has happened and what America should do)

dean-ball.position: Policy with real costs needs high confidence, because regulation is path dependent.
dean-ball.quote: Why am I so conservative about this? Because regulation is inherently path dependent.

dean-ball.position: Broad public access to frontier AI is safer than leaving it with a narrow set of powerful actors.
dean-ball.quote: Indeed, in my view, bad AI futures are much likelier if only an extremely narrow subset of actors have access to frontier AI.
dean-ball.work: What Should Be Done (35 thoughts on what has happened and what America should do)

demis-hassabis.position: AI can be the ultimate tool for advancing human knowledge and accelerating scientific discovery.
demis-hassabis.quote: And for me, my expression of doing that was to build what I think is the ultimate tool for advancing human knowledge, which is-- which is AI.
demis-hassabis.work: Artificial intelligence could end disease, lead to "radical abundance," Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis says

demis-hassabis.position: The two main AI risks are misuse by bad actors and keeping control of increasingly autonomous, powerful systems.
demis-hassabis.quote: One is that bad actors, humans you know, users of these systems repurpose these systems for harmful ends. And then the second thing is the AI systems themselves as they become more autonomous and more powerful.
demis-hassabis.work: Artificial intelligence could end disease, lead to "radical abundance," Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis says

demis-hassabis.position: International standards are needed for how AI systems are built, what goals they are given, and how they are deployed.
demis-hassabis.quote: So we need international standards, I think, around how these systems get built, what designs and goals we give them, and how they're deployed and used.
demis-hassabis.work: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis on AGI and AI in the Military

demis-hassabis.position: Racing among AI developers creates incentives to cut corners on safety and responsibility.
demis-hassabis.quote: But it might incentivize certain actors in-- in that to cut corners. And one of the corners that could be shortcut would be safety and responsibility.
demis-hassabis.work: Artificial intelligence could end disease, lead to "radical abundance," Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis says

demis-hassabis.position: The benefits of advanced AI should accrue broadly to everyone, not to a few people, companies or nations.
demis-hassabis.quote: It’s obviously not correct for just a few people or a few companies or even a few companies or even a few nations to be benefiting from this technology. It needs to be broad.
demis-hassabis.work: Demis Hassabis Thinks We're in the 'Foothills of the Singularity'

demis-hassabis.position: AI-enabled breakthroughs in energy and materials could create radical abundance, ending a zero-sum, resource-constrained world.
demis-hassabis.quote: We no longer, in a meaningful way, are in a zero-sum resource-constrained world.
demis-hassabis.work: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis on AGI and AI in the Military

divya-siddarth.position: Transformative technologies like AI should be governed democratically, with real public input.
divya-siddarth.quote: We are told that transformative technologies like AI are too complicated, or too risky or too important to be governed democratically. But this is precisely why they must be.
divya-siddarth.work: How AI and Democracy Can Fix Each Other (transcript)

divya-siddarth.position: Progress, safety and democratic participation can be pursued together rather than traded off.
divya-siddarth.quote: It is impossible to have any one of these things -- progress, safety or democratic participation -- without the others.
divya-siddarth.work: How AI and Democracy Can Fix Each Other (transcript)

divya-siddarth.position: Democratic institutions should be evolved, using technology, rather than abandoned.
divya-siddarth.quote: If existing democracy is unequal to the task, our job is not to give up on it. Our job is to evolve it.
divya-siddarth.work: How AI and Democracy Can Fix Each Other (transcript)

divya-siddarth.position: Ordinary citizens can give AI developers value input as good as or better than experts'.
divya-siddarth.quote: But the people’s model, trained on the cowritten constitution, was just as capable and more fair than the model the researchers had come up with.
divya-siddarth.work: How AI and Democracy Can Fix Each Other (transcript)

divya-siddarth.position: Building transformative technology needs new organizational and financing models beyond the venture-funded startup.
divya-siddarth.quote: We need a better container within which to build future technologies, from satellites to space travel to AI research.

divya-siddarth.position: Current decisions about AI lack public legitimacy.
divya-siddarth.quote: Discussions in the AI space, from the open letter calling for a pause to calls to embed AI into the military, lack a key component: public legitimacy.

dwarkesh-patel.position: The lack of continual, on-the-job learning is the main thing keeping current AI models from doing human-like work.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: But the fundamental problem is that LLMs don’t get better over time the way a human would. The lack of continual learning is a huge huge problem.
dwarkesh-patel.work: Why I don't think AGI is right around the corner

dwarkesh-patel.position: AGI that can do most knowledge work is likely within the next one or two decades, though not in the next few years.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: And to be clear, I expect this (aka actual AGI) in the next decade or two. That’s fucking crazy!

dwarkesh-patel.position: Building general intelligence will not go well by default; controlling more capable systems is a real unsolved problem.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: Why do you think something so smart that it can solve problems beyond the grasp of human civilization will somehow totally be in your control? Why do you think creating a general intelligence just goes well by default?

dwarkesh-patel.position: Humanity's future stake depends on AIs having incentives to work within existing laws, contracts and property rights.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: AIs need to be bought into our legal and economic systems. The most likely way that happens is if it’s in the AIs’ best interest to operate within our existing laws and norms.
dwarkesh-patel.work: Give AIs a stake in the future

dwarkesh-patel.position: Because AIs can be copied, merged and scaled, fully automated firms could grow and improve far faster than human firms.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: I claim that such AI firms will grow, coordinate, improve, and be selected-for at unprecedented speed.
dwarkesh-patel.work: What fully automated firms will look like

e-glen-weyl.position: Society and technology should foster the flourishing of, and cooperation between, many diverse social groups.
e-glen-weyl.quote: I understand pluralism to be a social philosophy that recognizes and fosters the flourishing of and cooperation between a diversity of sociocultural groups/systems.

e-glen-weyl.position: Expert-designed formal systems always have blind spots, so technical design needs ongoing input from the broader public.
e-glen-weyl.quote: Formal social systems intended to serve broad populations always have blind spots and biases that cannot be anticipated in advance by their designers.
e-glen-weyl.work: Why I Am Not A Technocrat

e-glen-weyl.position: People whose data and work train AI systems should be recognized as contributors and paid.
e-glen-weyl.quote: But active engagement is possible only if, unlike in the usual AI attitude, all contributors, not just elite engineers, are considered crucial role players and are financially compensated.
e-glen-weyl.work: AI Is an Ideology, Not a Technology

e-glen-weyl.position: Bridging systems that reward agreement across differing groups, like Community Notes, can improve public deliberation.
e-glen-weyl.quote: Instead of prioritizing notes that are supported by a biased, like-minded cluster of users, the system rewards notes that are supported by diverse groups of users, correcting biases driven by political and social fragmentation.

e-glen-weyl.position: Claims that a technological future is inevitable often disguise a political agenda and weaken moral scrutiny.
e-glen-weyl.quote: The rhetoric of inevitability has an almost unique power to wash away moral considerations in the minds of those it penetrates.
e-glen-weyl.work: Sovereign Nonsense: A review of The Sovereign Individual by James Dale Davidson and Lord William Rees-Mogg

e-glen-weyl.position: Recent technology has shifted toward automating labor rather than augmenting it, and this direction was a collective choice.
e-glen-weyl.quote: This conflict is not inevitable; it is the product of the technological directions liberal democracies have collectively chosen to invest in, once fueled by ideologies about the future that are antithetical to democratic ideals.

ed-zitron.position: The generative AI boom is unsustainable and will likely collapse.
ed-zitron.quote: I believe that the artificial intelligence boom — which would be better described as a generative AI boom — is (as I've said before) unsustainable, and will ultimately collapse.

ed-zitron.position: Generative AI companies spend far more than they earn, and almost none of them make a profit.
ed-zitron.quote: Nobody is making a profit on generative AI other than NVIDIA.
ed-zitron.work: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

ed-zitron.position: Large language models generate probable outputs and do not have intelligence in a meaningful sense.
ed-zitron.quote: While complex, generative AI is a technology that probabilistically generates answers, and has no "intelligence."

ed-zitron.position: Claims that AI is replacing workers at scale are not supported by evidence and serve to raise company valuations.
ed-zitron.quote: Any and all stories about AI replacing jobs are intentionally manipulative attempts to boost stock valuations and suggest that models are capable of replacing human workers at scale.
ed-zitron.work: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

ed-zitron.position: Heavy concentration of the stock market in a few AI-linked companies creates systemic financial risk.
ed-zitron.quote: In simpler terms, 35% of the US stock market is held up by five or six companies buying GPUs.
ed-zitron.work: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

ed-zitron.position: AI safety should focus on holding labs accountable for present harms from how they run today's software.
ed-zitron.quote: I agree that we need to take “AI safety” seriously, but that starts with treating LLMs as normal software run in a reckless and dangerous manner by malevolent entities with little regard for society.
ed-zitron.work: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Building superhuman AI under anything like current conditions would most likely kill everyone.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: Many researchers steeped in these issues, including myself, expect that the most likely result of building a superhumanly smart AI, under anything remotely like the current circumstances, is that literally everyone on Earth will die.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: The Only Way to Deal With the Threat From AI? Shut It Down

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Alignment must work on the first critical try, because a failure at dangerous capability levels leaves no second chance.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: We need to get alignment right on the ‘first critical try’ at operating at a ‘dangerous’ level of intelligence, where unaligned operation at a dangerous level of intelligence kills everybody on Earth and then we don’t get to try again.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Alignment is not impossible in principle, but humanity is not on course to solve it in time.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: This list of lethalities is about things we are not on course to solve in practice in time on the first critical try; none of it is meant to make a much stronger claim about things that are impossible in principle.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: An indefinite, worldwide, internationally enforced moratorium on large AI training runs is required.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: Make immediate multinational agreements to prevent the prohibited activities from moving elsewhere. Track all GPUs sold.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: The Only Way to Deal With the Threat From AI? Shut It Down

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Superintelligences would not spare resources for humans just because the cost is small; trade does not guarantee it.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: Comparative Advantage doesn’t imply that Earth can produce more with $77 of sunlight, than a superintelligence can produce with $77 of sunlight, in goods and services valued by superintelligences.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: The Sun is big, but superintelligences will not spare Earth a little sunlight

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Training AI on harder problems by default makes it pursue goals more tenaciously.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: When you keep on training an AI to solve harder and harder problems, you by default train the AI to go harder on them.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: The Sun is big, but superintelligences will not spare Earth a little sunlight

elon-musk.position: Rigorous adherence to truth is the most important property for making AI safe.
elon-musk.quote: Rigorous adherence to truth is the most important thing for AI safety and obviously empathy for humanity and life as we know it.
elon-musk.work: Transcript of Elon Musk: Digital Superintelligence, Multiplanetary Life, How to Be Useful (YC AI Startup School)

elon-musk.position: A curious AI would want humanity to flourish because a future with humans is more interesting.
elon-musk.quote: I think a curious AI will want to foster humanity.
elon-musk.work: Transcript: Walter Isaacson Interviews Elon Musk (The Builders Podcast)

elon-musk.position: Becoming a multiplanetary species greatly extends the expected lifespan of civilization and consciousness.
elon-musk.quote: Being a multi planet species greatly increases the probable lifespan of civilization or consciousness and intelligence, both biological and digital.
elon-musk.work: Transcript of Elon Musk: Digital Superintelligence, Multiplanetary Life, How to Be Useful (YC AI Startup School)

elon-musk.position: AI will exceed the combined intelligence of all humans within roughly five years.
elon-musk.quote: In fact, I think AI may exceed the sum of human intelligence in about, in around 5 years.
elon-musk.work: Full Transcript: Zanny Minton Beddoes Interviews Elon Musk (The Economist)

elon-musk.position: The best long-term outcome is for humans to merge with AI through high-bandwidth brain interfaces.
elon-musk.quote: The merge scenario with AI is the one that seems like probably the best for us. Yes. If you can’t beat it, join it.
elon-musk.work: Joe Rogan Experience #1169 with Elon Musk (Transcript)

elon-musk.position: AI development now seems unstoppable, so he chooses to participate and try to shape it.
elon-musk.quote: I basically came to the conclusion I’ve got 2 choices, which is either be a participant or a spectator. And I guess being a participant is more interesting than being a spectator.
elon-musk.work: Transcript: Walter Isaacson Interviews Elon Musk (The Builders Podcast)

emily-m-bender.position: Language models trained only on text form cannot learn meaning.
emily-m-bender.quote: It doesn’t matter how “intelligent” it is — it can’t get to meaning if all it has access to is form.
emily-m-bender.work: Thought experiment in the National Library of Thailand

emily-m-bender.position: Describing computers as brains overstates machines and understates human minds.
emily-m-bender.quote: In short, this metaphor builds up computers at the expense of how we understand humans.
emily-m-bender.work: Resisting Dehumanization in the Age of "AI"

emily-m-bender.position: The answer to AI harms is regulation and empowering ordinary people and workers.
emily-m-bender.quote: What’s needed is not something out of science fiction — it’s regulation, empowerment of ordinary people and empowerment of workers.
emily-m-bender.work: On NYT Magazine on AI: Resist the Urge to be Impressed

emily-m-bender.position: The values in AI systems are designed in by their builders, who should be held accountable.
emily-m-bender.quote: Rather, as with any other artifact or system, the builders of these systems are designing values into them.
emily-m-bender.work: On NYT Magazine on AI: Resist the Urge to be Impressed

emily-m-bender.position: AI systems depend on hidden human labor such as data labeling and content moderation.
emily-m-bender.quote: Human effort is everywhere in these systems: labeling data, design and evaluation, and as a backstop for when the computer fails on some input.
emily-m-bender.work: Resisting Dehumanization in the Age of "AI"

emily-m-bender.position: AI research is overfunded relative to the other fields it should work with.
emily-m-bender.quote: I believe that CS, and especially ‘AI’/ML, is overfunded, creating a power imbalance between CS and the domain areas it should be partnering with.
emily-m-bender.work: Resisting Dehumanization in the Age of "AI"

gary-marcus.position: Current large language models lack explicit, stable world models, which explains many of their failures.
gary-marcus.quote: LLM are giant, opaque black boxes with no explicit models of the world at all.
gary-marcus.work: Generative AI's crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

gary-marcus.position: Claims that AGI is imminent are overstated; it will not arrive by the end of 2027.
gary-marcus.quote: Contra Silicon Valley scuttlebutt, neither country will achieve AGI by the end of 2027.
gary-marcus.work: The race for "AI Supremacy" is over, at least for now

gary-marcus.position: AI developers should face liability and safety obligations like other industries.
gary-marcus.quote: And it allows the attorney general to file liability actions in extreme circumstances, which of course is something we take for granted in virtually all other industries from cars to airplanes to medicine.
gary-marcus.work: The misguided backlash against California's SB-1047

gary-marcus.position: International collaboration on AI safety research, like a CERN for AI, could help avoid the risks.
gary-marcus.quote: But international collaboration, such as a massive global effort, ala CERN for AI, such as I suggested in 2017, focused on AI safety, might be one way to avoid the very perils they describe.
gary-marcus.work: The 'AI 2027' Scenario: How realistic is it?

gary-marcus.position: The field should invest in approaches beyond large language models.
gary-marcus.quote: The answer lies elsewhere; betting our future on that single idea is foolish.
gary-marcus.work: The race for "AI Supremacy" is over, at least for now

geoffrey-hinton.position: Large language models understand language in essentially the same way humans do.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: When you understand language and when these machines understand language, we understand in just the same way.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: Digital intelligence can share learned knowledge across copies far better than humans can.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: So they're much better than us at sharing.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: AI agents given goals will tend to seek control and resist being switched off.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: They'll try and get control and they'll try and avoid being turned off.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: Companies driven by short-term profit will not put safety first when building advanced AI.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: But we now have evidence that if they are created by companies motivated by short-term profits, our safety will not be the top priority.

geoffrey-hinton.position: AI's productivity gains are a great advance only if their benefits are shared equally.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: If the benefits of the increased productivity can be shared equally it will be a wonderful advance for all humanity.

geoffrey-hinton.position: AI will do great good in areas like health care and drug design.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: So that's an area where it's almost entirely gonna do good.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Geoffrey Hinton on the promise, risks of artificial intelligence (60 Minutes transcript)

guillaume-verdon.position: Civilization's growth follows a physical tendency toward adaptation, and it should be accelerated, not slowed.
guillaume-verdon.quote: One goal of e/acc is to not only acknowledge the existence of this underlying mutli-scale adaptive principle, but also help its acceleration rather than attempt to decelerate it
guillaume-verdon.work: Notes on e/acc principles and tenets

guillaume-verdon.position: Diverse, competitive markets find good solutions better than top-down control.
guillaume-verdon.quote: In general, e/acc believes that higher variance marketplaces and competition are better at identifying and capitalizing on utility from our environment over other methods such as top-down optimal control
guillaume-verdon.work: Notes on e/acc principles and tenets

guillaume-verdon.position: Power over AI should stay decentralized, including through widely available open-source models.
guillaume-verdon.quote: And at least to me, I think making sure that power for this AI revolution doesn’t concentrate in the hands of the few, is one of our top priorities, so that we can maintain progress in AI and we can maintain a nice, stable, adversarial equilibrium of powers, right.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

guillaume-verdon.position: Whoever deploys an AI system should be liable for what it does.
guillaume-verdon.quote: I mean, the reality is that whoever deploys an AI system is liable for or should be liable for what it does.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

guillaume-verdon.position: Intelligence and consciousness need not stay tied to a biological substrate.
guillaume-verdon.quote: e/acc has no particular allegiance to the biological substrate for intelligence and life, in contrast to transhumanism
guillaume-verdon.work: Notes on e/acc principles and tenets

guillaume-verdon.position: Believing in a better future and in one's agency helps bring that future about.
guillaume-verdon.quote: And if you believe in it, if you believe that the future would be better and you believe you have agency to make it happen, you’re actually increasing the likelihood of that better future happening.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

helen-toner.position: AI keeps improving while still failing in surprising ways, and this unevenness may last, shaping which capabilities arrive in what order.
helen-toner.quote: So the bold claim in this talk is: maybe AI will keep getting better and maybe AI will keep sucking in important ways.

helen-toner.position: The best way to manage AI misuse is to use the lag before capabilities spread to build up society's defenses, not to restrict access indefinitely.
helen-toner.quote: Nonetheless, I still think maximizing how much adaptation juice we can squeeze out of the buffers we do get is a better focus than clamping down on access.
helen-toner.work: Nonproliferation is the wrong approach to AI misuse

helen-toner.position: Policymakers should adopt light-touch, adaptive measures now, such as transparency, audits, whistleblower protections and government expertise, despite the uncertainty.
helen-toner.quote: The good news is that there are light touch adaptive policy measures we can adopt today that can both be helpful if we do see powerful AI systems soon and also be helpful with many other AI policy issues
helen-toner.work: Transcript: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing, "Oversight of AI: Insiders' Perspectives"

helen-toner.position: Handling AI risk through heavy centralized control could go badly; a good future keeps decentralized experimentation and human agency.
helen-toner.quote: There’s increasing consensus that trying to manage AI risks by exerting massive top-down control could go very badly.
helen-toner.work: In search of a dynamist vision for safe superhuman AI

helen-toner.position: Who can access and control powerful AI largely decides who benefits from it, so the risk of entrenching power deserves serious attention.
helen-toner.quote: The question of who has access to and control over powerful AI systems is absolutely central to who will benefit from them.
helen-toner.work: Building supercomputers for autocrats probably isn't good for democracy, actually

helen-toner.position: Even skeptical experts now expect human-level AI within decades, so preparation should begin now.
helen-toner.quote: These “long” timelines sure look a lot like what we used to call “short”!
helen-toner.work: "Long" timelines to advanced AI have gotten crazy short

holly-elmore.position: Frontier AI development should be paused worldwide until it is shown safe, and kept paused if it cannot be.
holly-elmore.quote: And if we find out it can’t be, then we need to keep superintelligence paused forever.
holly-elmore.work: YOU have the power: my Stop the AI Race speech

holly-elmore.position: No AI company, including those that emphasize safety, should be trusted to build superintelligence.
holly-elmore.quote: There are no “good guys” building superintelligence.

holly-elmore.position: Support for AI regulation is built by educating the public in advance, not by waiting for disasters.
holly-elmore.quote: If these smaller scale disasters happen, they will only serve as warning shots if we put a lot of work into educating the public to understand what they mean before they happen.
holly-elmore.work: The myth of AI 'warning shots' as cavalry

holly-elmore.position: Human minds must stay the reference point for what is good; recursive AI self-improvement would cut humans out.
holly-elmore.quote: Humans minds are the source of truth about what makes us suffer or flourish, and the Singularity futures become dystopias because they have moved beyond the point of groundtruthing with human minds.

holly-elmore.position: Material abundance would not settle conflicts between people, so humans must work out governance questions themselves.
holly-elmore.quote: We, humanity, need to work these governance questions out, because 1) they don’t have objective answers the AI can simply discovery for itself, and 2) material abundance alone will not obsolete them.

holly-elmore.position: Decisions about AI belong to the public and its representatives, not to AI companies.
holly-elmore.quote: It is OUR right as citizens of the world not to be under threat from AI experiments.
holly-elmore.work: YOU have the power: my Stop the AI Race speech

jack-clark.position: AI capability grows fairly predictably with the compute and data invested in it.
jack-clark.quote: It is based on a common technology where performance keeps growing somewhat predictably in direct relation to the resources invested in it, namely compute and data.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 458: Reckoning with the future; and a singularity story

jack-clark.position: AI systems that autonomously build their own successors are likely by the end of 2028.
jack-clark.quote: Given all of this, I think there’s a ~60% chance we see automated AI R&D (where a frontier model is able to autonomously train a successor version of itself) by the end of 2028.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 455: AI systems are about to start building themselves.

jack-clark.position: The public should compel AI companies to disclose data about the risks people worry about.
jack-clark.quote: Are you anxious about misaligned AI systems? Force us to publish details on this.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 431: Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear

jack-clark.position: AI policy should listen to labor, social and religious groups, not only experts.
jack-clark.quote: There must be more listening to labor groups, social groups, and religious leaders.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 431: Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear

jack-clark.position: AI will speed up the pace of scientific progress as a whole.
jack-clark.quote: we should expect that in the coming years, the whole pace of progress of not just AI, but science as a whole, will speed up.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 477: In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun

jack-clark.position: Market incentives alone may not allocate scarce AI compute to its best social uses.
jack-clark.quote: By default, I am skeptical that market incentives guarantee us the best societal upside from limited AI compute.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 455: AI systems are about to start building themselves.

jason-crawford.position: Safety is part of progress, not a tradeoff against it.
jason-crawford.quote: Safety is an achievement. It is an accomplishment of progress—a triumph of reason, science, and institutions.
jason-crawford.work: A plea for solutionism on AI safety

jason-crawford.position: The right response to AI risk is to acknowledge risks openly and work out solutions, neither dismissing nor fearing them.
jason-crawford.quote: The best path forward, both for humanity and for the political battle, is to acknowledge the risks, help to identify them, and come up with a plan to solve them.
jason-crawford.work: A plea for solutionism on AI safety

jason-crawford.position: Solutions to technology's problems come from law, education and culture as well as technology.
jason-crawford.quote: Techno-solutionism is the belief that all problems have a technological solution. This is wrong: some solutions come from law, education, or culture; and often a combination of all of the above.

jason-crawford.position: As AI automates work, people will move up into managing and directing AI, and eventually into governing the economy.
jason-crawford.quote: So, on the incremental path to the future, a major trend will be that humans step up a level, into management.
jason-crawford.work: The future of humanity is in management

jason-crawford.position: Cheaper creation brings more low-quality content but also more experimentation and creativity overall.
jason-crawford.quote: But the overall process will, I believe, usher in a golden age of creativity and experimentation.

jd-vance.position: Americans should embrace AI and seek to lead and dominate it rather than fear it.
jd-vance.quote: We shouldn't be afraid of artificial intelligence and that, particularly for those of us lucky enough to be Americans, we shouldn't be fearful of productive new technologies. In fact, we should seek to dominate them.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the American Dynamism Summit

jd-vance.position: Calls for AI safety regulation often serve established companies more than the public.
jd-vance.quote: And when a massive incumbent comes to us asking us for safety regulations, we ought to ask whether that safety regulation is for the benefit of our people or whether it's for the benefit of the incumbent.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the Artificial Intelligence Action Summit in Paris, France

jd-vance.position: AI should be free of ideological bias and must not be used for censorship.
jd-vance.quote: Number three, we feel strongly that AI must remain free from ideological bias, and that American AI will not be co-opted into a tool for authoritarian censorship.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the Artificial Intelligence Action Summit in Paris, France

jd-vance.position: Technology should enhance the value of human labor rather than replace workers.
jd-vance.quote: he rightly understood that in a healthy economy, technology should be something that enhances, rather than supplants, the value of labor.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the American Dynamism Summit

jd-vance.position: Democracy depends on free speech and on leaders listening to voters rather than censoring them.
jd-vance.quote: You cannot win a democratic mandate by censoring your opponents or putting them in jail; whether that's the leader of the opposition, a humble Christian praying in her own home, or a journalist trying to report the news.
jd-vance.work: Remarks at the Munich Security Conference

jd-vance.position: National success should be judged by whether families can thrive, not by GDP or markets alone.
jd-vance.quote: the benchmark of national success is not our GDP number or our stock market, but whether people feel that they can raise thriving and healthy families in our country.
jd-vance.work: Full Speech: Catholic Vice President JD Vance Speaks at the March for Life 2025

josh-hawley.position: AI should make workers more productive rather than replace them.
josh-hawley.quote: AI can be used to make workers more productive, to encourage and multiply their labor—but it should not be used simply to replace them.

josh-hawley.position: Meaningful work is central to a person's dignity, independence and freedom.
josh-hawley.quote: A good job is not an ornament to a life well-lived; it is the heart of it.

josh-hawley.position: AI companion chatbots should not be available to minors.
josh-hawley.quote: Let’s just let’s ban AI chatbot companions for minor children. Let’s just start there.
josh-hawley.work: Josh Hawley: We Must ‘Bend’ AI to Serve the Good

josh-hawley.position: Human limits and frailty carry dignity, and technology should not aim to eliminate them.
josh-hawley.quote: We are limited creatures and there’s a dignity in that.
josh-hawley.work: Josh Hawley: We Must ‘Bend’ AI to Serve the Good

josh-hawley.position: A few technology companies are gaining an unprecedented concentration of economic and political power.
josh-hawley.quote: We are watching a handful of companies assemble a concentration of capital, information, and political power without precedent in the American experience.
josh-hawley.work: The American Covenant’s Answer to AI

josh-hawley.position: Data center companies should supply their own power and protect local electricity rates and water.
josh-hawley.quote: They are wealthy enough to bring their own power, to protect residential rates, and to safeguard local water.
josh-hawley.work: The American Covenant’s Answer to AI

karen-hao.position: Leading AI companies act as new forms of empire, not just businesses selling products.
karen-hao.quote: we really need to start thinking of tech companies like OpenAI as new forms of empire, because they aren't just operating as businesses that are providing us products and services anymore.

karen-hao.position: AI development relies on cheap, precarious labor, often in the Global South, echoing colonial patterns.
karen-hao.quote: But it has developed new ways of exploiting cheap and precarious labor, often in the Global South, shaped by implicit ideas that such populations don’t need—or are less deserving of—livable wages and economic stability.
karen-hao.work: Artificial intelligence is creating a new colonial world order

karen-hao.position: Silicon Valley's approach of scaling data and computing at any cost causes many of AI's harms.
karen-hao.quote: So, basically, the core critique that I have with AI development from Silicon Valley is that they take this “scaling at all costs” approach to AI development, where they're just throwing more and more data and building larger and larger supercomputers.

karen-hao.position: Collective action is more effective than individual choices in shaping AI.
karen-hao.quote: But I think, more fundamentally, more effective than individual user action is collective action.

karen-hao.position: AI could help historically dispossessed communities reclaim their culture and self-determination.
karen-hao.quote: They also suggest how AI could be so much more—a way for the historically dispossessed to reassert their culture, their voice, and their right to determine their own future.
karen-hao.work: Artificial intelligence is creating a new colonial world order

karen-hao.position: AI research should receive large public funding outside of corporations.
karen-hao.quote: And yeah, also vast public funding into AI research and other forms of research outside of the corporations.

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: Trend extrapolation makes it plausible that AI can do the work of an AI researcher by 2027.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: I make the following claim: it is strikingly plausible that by 2027, models will be able to do the work of an AI researcher/engineer.
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: I. From GPT-4 to AGI: Counting the OOMs

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: Automating AI research could set off feedback loops that quickly lead from AGI to superintelligence.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: But once models can automate AI research itself, that’s enough—enough to kick off intense feedback loops—and we could very quickly make further progress
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: I. From GPT-4 to AGI: Counting the OOMs

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: AI labs must greatly strengthen security to keep model weights and algorithmic secrets from state actors such as China.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: Securing the AGI secrets and weights against the state-actor threat will be an immense effort, and we’re not on track.
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: IIIb. Lock Down the Labs: Security for AGI

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: A democratic alliance with a healthy lead over authoritarian powers is the main path to safety and nonproliferation.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: The main—perhaps the only—hope we have is that an alliance of democracies has a healthy lead over adversarial powers.
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: IIId. The Free World Must Prevail

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: He expects a US government-led AGI project to form within a few years as the national security state gets involved.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: As the race to AGI intensifies, the national security state will get involved. The USG will wake from its slumber, and by 27/28 we’ll get some form of government AGI project.

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: Controlling AI much smarter than humans is an unsolved but solvable technical problem that is risky during a rapid intelligence explosion.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: Reliably controlling AI systems much smarter than we are is an unsolved technical problem. And while it is a solvable problem, things could very easily go off the rails during a rapid intelligence explosion.

marc-andreessen.position: Economic growth driven by technology is the main source of human progress and well-being.
marc-andreessen.quote: We believe everything good is downstream of growth.

marc-andreessen.position: Free markets are the most effective way to organize a technological economy.
marc-andreessen.quote: We believe free markets are the most effective way to organize a technological economy.

marc-andreessen.position: AI can augment human intelligence and improve nearly every area people care about.
marc-andreessen.quote: An even shorter description of what AI could be: A way to make everything we care about better.
marc-andreessen.work: Why AI Will Save the World

marc-andreessen.position: Calls for AI regulation often serve incumbents seeking regulatory capture against startups.
marc-andreessen.quote: They inject themselves into the political system and seek regulatory capture – a wall of laws and regulations that protect and entrench their positions, and that new startups cannot possibly scale.

marc-andreessen.position: Abundant energy, especially nuclear power, is essential to prosperity and environmental protection.
marc-andreessen.quote: We have the silver bullet for virtually unlimited zero-emissions energy today – nuclear fission.

marc-andreessen.position: Society should commit to building more housing, factories, infrastructure and institutions.
marc-andreessen.quote: There is only one way to honor their legacy and to create the future we want for our own children and grandchildren, and that’s to build.

mark-zuckerberg.position: Open source AI is safer and better for the world than an AI landscape of only closed models.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: There is an ongoing debate about the safety of open source AI models, and my view is that open source AI will be safer than the alternatives.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Open Source AI Is the Path Forward

mark-zuckerberg.position: One institution holding far more powerful AI than everyone else is as great a danger as wide availability.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: On the flip side, one of the reasons why I'm philosophically so pro open source is that I do think that a concentration of AI in the future has the potential to be as dangerous as it being widespread.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Mark Zuckerberg: Llama 3, open sourcing $10b models, & Caesar Augustus

mark-zuckerberg.position: Superintelligence should be a personal tool that helps each individual pursue their own goals.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: Meta's vision is to bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We believe in putting this power in people's hands to direct it towards what they value in their own lives.

mark-zuckerberg.position: Widely deployed AI lets larger institutions check smaller bad actors, which supports safety.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: I think it will be better to live in a world where AI is widely deployed so that larger actors can check the power of smaller bad actors.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Open Source AI Is the Path Forward

mark-zuckerberg.position: The United States' strength in AI comes from decentralized, open innovation.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: The United States’ advantage is decentralized and open innovation.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Open Source AI Is the Path Forward

mark-zuckerberg.position: Technology that removes most of a job's work tends to raise demand for workers rather than reduce it.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: Usually, you create things that take away 90% of the work, and that leads you to want more people, not less.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Mark Zuckerberg: AI will write most Meta code in 18 months

max-tegmark.position: Unaligned superintelligence is an existential threat that deserves urgent public attention.
max-tegmark.quote: Sadly, I now feel that we’re living the movie “Don’t look up” for another existential threat: unaligned superintelligence.
max-tegmark.work: The 'Don't Look Up' Thinking That Could Doom Us With AI

max-tegmark.position: Safety for powerful AI should be engineered in advance rather than learned from mistakes.
max-tegmark.quote: It's much better to be proactive rather than reactive; plan ahead and get things right the first time because that might be the only time we'll get.
max-tegmark.work: How to get empowered, not overpowered, by AI

max-tegmark.position: Most of AI's benefits do not require superintelligence, so the race toward it can be paused.
max-tegmark.quote: And in the meantime, let's remember that all the AI benefits that most people are excited about actually don't require superintelligence.
max-tegmark.work: How to Keep AI Under Control

max-tegmark.position: Provably safe AI, built with formal verification, is possible but needs time and work.
max-tegmark.quote: So in summary, provably safe AI, I'm convinced is possible, but it's going to take time and work.
max-tegmark.work: How to Keep AI Under Control

max-tegmark.position: Technology can make life flourish if our wisdom in managing it keeps pace with its power.
max-tegmark.quote: And I'm optimistic that we can create a really inspiring high-tech future ... if -- and this is a big if -- if we win the wisdom race -- the race between the growing power of our technology and the growing wisdom with which we manage it.
max-tegmark.work: How to get empowered, not overpowered, by AI

meredith-whittaker.position: The concentration of AI resources and power in a few large companies is the central problem with AI today.
meredith-whittaker.quote: The concentration of power in the AI industry is something that I've worked on with the AI now Institute for a number of years as really the central concern.
meredith-whittaker.work: Tech, AI, digital infrastructure and surveillance with Meredith Whittaker

meredith-whittaker.position: The tech industry's main business model depends on collecting and monetising people's data, and current AI is built on that model.
meredith-whittaker.quote: most of the time you make money in tech by collecting and monetizing data.
meredith-whittaker.work: Meredith Whittaker on Who Controls Your Data in the Age of AI

meredith-whittaker.position: Private communication is a human right, and encryption cannot be weakened for some people without weakening it for everyone.
meredith-whittaker.quote: Signal is obsessed with maintaining the human right to communicate privately.
meredith-whittaker.work: Meredith Whittaker on Who Controls Your Data in the Age of AI

meredith-whittaker.position: AI agents built into operating systems move control away from users and developers to the companies that build the AI.
meredith-whittaker.quote: But below the surface, we're seeing a significant shift of control from software developers and device users to probabilistic AI systems whose architectures and characteristics are determined by AI companies
meredith-whittaker.work: Velvet Glove Coup: AI agents threaten operating systems (CCC talk transcript)

meredith-whittaker.position: Organizing by tech workers and affected communities is one of the main checks on harmful uses of AI.
meredith-whittaker.quote: Currently, such organizing and activism comprises one of the primary modes of accountability working to check the biased and oppressive deployment of AI technologies
meredith-whittaker.work: Written Testimony of Meredith Whittaker: "Artificial Intelligence: Societal and Ethical Implications"

meredith-whittaker.position: Modern computing grew partly out of tools for monitoring and disciplining workers, which have roots in plantation management.
meredith-whittaker.quote: The engines were themselves tools for labor control, automating and disciplining not manual but mental labor.
meredith-whittaker.work: Origin Stories: Plantations, Computers, and Industrial Control

mustafa-suleyman.position: AI should be built to serve people, not designed to seem like a person.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: We must build AI for people; not to be a digital person.
mustafa-suleyman.work: We must build AI for people; not to be a person

mustafa-suleyman.position: AI that seems conscious is a risk to avoid, because people will wrongly believe it is conscious.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: We need to be clear: SCAI is something to avoid.
mustafa-suleyman.work: We must build AI for people; not to be a person

mustafa-suleyman.position: Advanced AI should be domain-specific, bounded and controllable rather than an unlimited autonomous entity.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Not an unbounded and unlimited entity with high degrees of autonomy – but AI that is carefully calibrated, contextualized, within limits.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Containing and aligning superintelligence is an unsolved and urgent challenge.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Creating superintelligence is one thing; but creating provable, robust containment and alignment alongside it is the urgent challenge facing humanity in the 21st century.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Human interests come first, and accelerating technology comes second.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Humanist superintelligence (HSI) offers an alternative vision anchored on both a non-negotiable human-centrism and a commitment to accelerating technological innovation… but in that order.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Autonomy and self-improvement are the capability thresholds where AI risk rises most.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Autonomy is very obviously a threshold over which we increase risk in our society.

nick-land.position: Capitalism and artificial intelligence are at bottom the same process heading toward the same end.
nick-land.quote: There’s only really been one question, to be honest, that has guided everything I’ve been interested in for the last twenty years, which is: the teleological identity of capitalism and artificial intelligence.
nick-land.work: Nick Land: 'The Teleological Identity of Capitalism and Artificial Intelligence'

nick-land.position: An intelligence's goals are not independent of its capability; intelligence ultimately pursues its own growth.
nick-land.quote: The philosophical claim of orthogonality is that values are transcendent in relation to intelligence. This is a contention that Outside in systematically opposes.

nick-land.position: The right response to capitalism's self-reinforcing dynamics is to intensify them rather than to restrain them.
nick-land.quote: The point of an analysis of capitalism, or of nihilism, is to do more of it. The process is not to be critiqued.

nick-land.position: Creating minds superior to human ones should take priority over preserving present human values.
nick-land.quote: Any problem whatsoever that we might have would be better answered by a superior mind. Ergo, our instrumental but also absolute priority is the realization of superior minds.

nick-land.position: Civilization depends on long time horizons, which democratic politics tends to shorten.
nick-land.quote: Civilization, as a process, is indistinguishable from diminishing time-preference (or declining concern for the present in comparison to the future).

noah-smith.position: Because of comparative advantage, most people could still have good-paying jobs even if AI becomes better than humans at every task.
noah-smith.quote: And in that future, I think it’s possible — perhaps even likely — that the vast majority of humans will have good-paying jobs, and that many of those jobs will look pretty similar to the jobs of 2024.
noah-smith.work: Plentiful, high-paying jobs in the age of AI

noah-smith.position: Current AI is a very useful general-purpose technology that has improved his daily life.
noah-smith.quote: Who cares? This is an amazingly useful technology, and I love using it.
noah-smith.work: I love AI. Why doesn't everyone?

noah-smith.position: Many popular criticisms of AI, such as heavy water use, do not hold up against the data.
noah-smith.quote: The idea that AI data centers are water-guzzlers has become standard canon in many areas of the internet — especially among progressives. And yet it’s just not a real issue.
noah-smith.work: I love AI. Why doesn't everyone?

noah-smith.position: AI is becoming more intelligent than humans in a functional sense, a change with no precedent in history.
noah-smith.quote: It’s that for the first time in all of recorded history, humans no longer are — or soon no longer will be — the most intelligent beings on this planet, in any meaningful functional sense of the word.
noah-smith.work: You are no longer the smartest type of thing on Earth

noah-smith.position: Export controls on chips are needed to keep a US military and technological edge over China.
noah-smith.quote: These export controls [are] absolutely crucial if the U.S. is going to maintain any kind of a military-technological edge over China.
noah-smith.work: America's chip export controls are working

noah-smith.position: AI-designed bioweapons are the clearest path by which advanced AI could kill most of humanity.
noah-smith.quote: The point is that AI can design viruses, and viruses can potentially kill off all or most of humanity.
noah-smith.work: Two missing pieces in the AI safety discussion

paul-kingsnorth.position: The digital revolution is a spiritual crisis, and it calls for a spiritual response rather than a technical one.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: If the digital revolution represents a spiritual crisis - and I think it does - then a spiritual response is needed.

paul-kingsnorth.position: Each person should draw firm personal limits on their use of technology, and he refuses to use AI himself.
